docs.title: Who runs the server?
docs.text:
The server is owned and operated exclusively by Auzer1 and FunOD. There are no other moderators, admins, or staff members.

If someone claims 'staff powers' in-game

They are attempting to deceive you. No hidden or alt staff accounts exist. See Rules → Verified Authority.

docs.title: Is there an official Discord?
docs.text: No. There is no official Discord server, and there are no plans to create one. Many player-run communities exist, but none of them are moderated or sanctioned by us.

docs.title: Is cheating or exploiting allowed?
docs.text: Exploiting isn't punishable, but is automatically prevented by the AntiCheat where possible. Any exploits that bypass the AntiCheat aren't punishable either.

docs.title: Why is your version of Cobblemon different from Cobbleverse?
docs.text:
We removed the ambience mods, shader mods, and other graphics-enhancement mods from the pack. Content — Pokémon, mechanics, structures, progression — is intact. What's gone is the visual bloat that makes the official pack unplayable on lower-end hardware.

The point is inclusivity: anyone with a modest laptop should be able to play here. We measure success in "does it run at 60 FPS on 4 GB RAM," not "does it have the prettiest fog." This is the same reason our other servers (anarchy and Cursed Walking) also run modified, cracked-friendly setups.

docs.title: Are there plans to increase the player limit?
docs.text: Not at the moment. We prefer to keep the server manageable and within a resource range we can personally oversee.

docs.title: Which modpack does the server run?
docs.text:
The server uses AutoModpack, which means the client doesn't need a fixed static modpack — whichever mods and resource packs the server is currently running are pulled down automatically when you connect. You have three install paths (all covered on the Install page):

  • A pre-built AutoModpack base (fastest).
  • Adding AutoModpack to your own Fabric instance.
  • A standard CurseForge-format modpack that installs everything at once (no live sync — for players who prefer a static setup).

Or you can install every file manually. The list of required mods is fetched live on the Install page from the server itself.

docs.title: Which Minecraft version?
docs.text: Minecraft 1.21.1, matching Cobblemon's supported version. We plan to stay here for a while — Cobblemon's release cadence means the pack is stable on 1.21.1 for the foreseeable future. Match it exactly when installing Fabric; adjacent Minecraft versions won't connect.

docs.title: How much RAM does my machine need?
docs.text: Allocate at least 4 GB to the instance. Less than 4 GB and you'll stutter through chunk loads.

docs.title: Do I have to use the exact pack we provide?
docs.text: For the server-required mods, yes — the server checks that Fabric API, Cobblemon, and the rest of the sync list match. Adding client-side-only mods (shaders, minimap, cosmetics) is fine as long as they don't affect server sync. If you're using AutoModpack, your own additions live in your regular .minecraft/mods/ folder and don't conflict with what AutoModpack downloads.

docs.title: Where's the full mod list?
docs.text: On the Install page — it's fetched live from the server (reading each mod jar's metadata directly), so it stays in sync with what's actually installed on the server.

docs.title: What launchers are supported?
docs.text: Any launcher that can install Fabric. The Install page has four setup paths — the AutoModpack routes work with any launcher (including SKLauncher and TLauncher), and the standard-modpack route works with any CurseForge-aware launcher (CurseForge, ATLauncher, Prism, GDLauncher, MultiMC). Offline / cracked accounts are supported.

docs.title: The launcher says "outdated client" or "outdated server"
docs.text: Version mismatch. Check the server's current version in the status box and reinstall the Fabric loader / modpack for that exact Minecraft version.

docs.title: Still have a question?
docs.text: Head to the Support page to reach an admin.

docs.title: Installing the Modpack
docs.text:
Everything you need to get on the server. Pick whichever setup approach suits you — all four end with you on the server, and the server ships with AutoModpack so any of them stays in sync automatically once you connect.

This is not the pack you'd install from Modrinth or CurseForge. We removed ambience mods, shader mods, and other graphics-heavy additions so the pack runs at around 60 FPS on 8 GB RAM on typical machines. Content mirrors Cobbleverse; the visual bloat doesn't. Because of this, installing the official pack will not let you join — you'll get rejected on the connection mod check. Use one of the setup paths below to get our version instead.

Which method should I pick?

  • New to modded Minecraft, or you just want to play? → Method 1 (pre-built AutoModpack pack).
  • Already have a Fabric instance you like? → Method 2 (add AutoModpack to it).
  • Prefer a static, self-contained install? → Method 3 (standard modpack).
  • Want total control over every file? → Method 4 (manual).

docs.title: How to Join
docs.text:
1. Pre-built AutoModpack modpack (easiest)2. Add AutoModpack to your own instance3. Standard modpack (no AutoModpack)4. Fully manual

This is a clean Fabric instance with AutoModpack pre-installed and the required client-side resource packs already in place. Once launched, connecting to the server pulls in everything else automatically. Nothing to configure.

Download: Cobblemon Server – AutoModpack Base (.zip)

Steps (any CurseForge-aware launcher):

  1. In your launcher, choose Import modpack (or Add instance → From .zip).
  2. Select the downloaded .zip.
  3. Wait for the launcher to build the instance.
  4. Launch the instance.
  5. Multiplayer → Add Server, enter the server IP from the home page.
  6. On first connect, AutoModpack asks you to verify the server's certificate fingerprint. Confirm it.
  7. AutoModpack downloads the current modpack. When it's done, restart Minecraft. Done.

For SKLauncher / TLauncher (no CurseForge-format import): Extract the .zip manually and copy the mods/, config/, and resourcepacks/ folders into your Fabric profile's .minecraft folder. Then launch that Fabric profile. If you'd rather skip the pre-built pack entirely, the Fully manual tab has step-by-step instructions.

If you already have a working Fabric instance (any version, any launcher), you don't need any of our downloads. Just install AutoModpack and connect.

Steps:

  1. Install Fabric Loader for the Minecraft version the server is running (check the status box on the home page).
  2. Install Fabric API for the same version. Grab it from Modrinth or CurseForge and place the .jar in your instance's mods/ folder.
  3. Download AutoModpack from Modrinth or CurseForge. Match the Minecraft version.
  4. Drop the AutoModpack .jar into the same mods/ folder.
  5. Launch the instance.
  6. Multiplayer → Add Server, enter the server IP from the home page.
  7. On first connect: verify the server's fingerprint → confirm the modpack install → wait for the download → restart Minecraft.

Your own mods stay untouched

AutoModpack downloads the server's synced files into ~/.minecraft/automodpack/modpacks/…, isolated from your instance's regular mods/ folder. Any client-side-only mods you've added — minimaps, shader loaders, cosmetic mods — keep working alongside the synced modpack.

Even quicker: AutoModpack's own Fabric installer

AutoModpack ships a modified Fabric installer that installs Fabric loader and AutoModpack in one step. If you're setting up a fresh instance from scratch, that saves you steps 1–4 above.

A regular CurseForge-format modpack containing a modlist.html — your launcher fetches every mod from Modrinth and CurseForge at import time and locks the versions in. Once installed, you connect like it's a vanilla server. No live sync; when the server updates its mods, you'll need to reimport a new version of this pack.

Download: Cobblemon Server – Standard Modpack (.zip)

Steps (CurseForge, ATLauncher, Prism, GDLauncher, or MultiMC):

  1. In your launcher, choose Import modpack (or Add instance → From .zip).
  2. Select the downloaded .zip.
  3. The launcher reads the modlist.html/manifest.json and downloads every mod from its source. This usually takes a few minutes.
  4. Launch the instance.
  5. Multiplayer → Add Server, enter the server IP from the home page.

SKLauncher / TLauncher don't import CurseForge modpacks natively

For those launchers, use one of the CurseForge-aware launchers above just for the import step, then point your usual launcher at the resulting instance folder. Or switch to the Fully manual tab above.

Install every mod and resource pack by hand. Most control, most work. The lists further down this page are the source of truth — copy every mod's .jar into your instance's mods/ folder and every resource pack's .zip into resourcepacks/.

Steps:

  1. In your launcher, install Fabric Loader for the Minecraft version the server is running (check the status box).
  2. Install Fabric API — put its .jar into your instance's mods/ folder.
  3. From the Required mods section below, download each mod's .jar (match the correct Minecraft version). Drop them all into mods/.
  4. From the Required resource packs section below, download each .zip and drop them into resourcepacks/.
  5. Launch the instance. In Minecraft's Options → Resource Packs, enable each pack.
  6. Multiplayer → Add Server, enter the server IP from the home page.

Your Minecraft instance folder is usually at:

C:\Users\%USERNAME%\AppData\Roaming\.minecraft

On some launchers (Prism, MultiMC) the profile has its own minecraft/ folder inside the instance directory. Check your launcher's docs if you're unsure.

docs.title: Verifying it Worked
docs.text:
Once the game loads:

  • Bottom-left of the main menu shows Fabric API (and, if you used AutoModpack, an AutoModpack notice).
  • The main menu has a Mods button showing the mod list.
  • Server IP appears as compatible in your multiplayer list.
  • If you connected via AutoModpack, the first connection prompts a fingerprint check and a modpack confirmation before downloading.

If any of these are missing, jump to Troubleshooting below.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
\"Outdated server\" or \"Outdated client\" in the multiplayer list

Your Fabric profile is running a different Minecraft version than the server. Check the version in the home page status box and reinstall Fabric for that exact version.

Game crashes on launch

Usually a mismatch between the pack version and the Minecraft version. Reinstall the pack (or reinstall Fabric + redownload mods) for the version the server is currently running.

\"Server modded, this client is vanilla\"

Fabric loaded, but no mods did. Double-check that your mods/ folder ended up in the actual profile folder your launcher uses. In SKLauncher/TLauncher, this is usually .minecraft; in Prism/MultiMC it's inside the instance's minecraft/ subfolder.

AutoModpack asks about a certificate fingerprint — is that safe?

Yes. AutoModpack encrypts its downloads and asks you to verify the server on first connect so nobody can substitute their own modpack. Just confirm and it'll remember for future connects.

AutoModpack downloaded the pack but the game is still \"vanilla\"

You need to restart Minecraft after the download finishes. AutoModpack loads the downloaded modpack on next launch — not mid-session.

The modpack I imported has no mods after install

Some CurseForge packs only ship a manifest.json for licensing reasons. Use a CurseForge-aware launcher (CurseForge, ATLauncher, Prism, GDLauncher) — those fetch the actual mod files automatically. SKLauncher and TLauncher can't do this on their own.

The mod list on this page didn't load

The list is fetched from the server's /api/modlist endpoint. If the API is unreachable — server offline, network hiccup — the list won't render. Use one of the AutoModpack methods above in the meantime; they don't rely on this list.

docs.title: Welcome to the Cobblemon Server
docs.text: The new modded server is live. This is a fresh start — new world, new rules to test-drive, and the same principles as before.

docs.title: What's Different
docs.text:
• Modpack: Cobblemon Official Modpack [Fabric] by CobbledStudios. Fabric loader, Minecraft 1.21.1 (see the home page for the current version).
  • Setup: Beta phase — expect bugs, mod tweaks, and occasional downtime while things settle.
  • Uptime: May not be 24/7 in the first weeks.

docs.title: What Carried Over
docs.text:
• Your account and login work as-is. No re-registering.
  • The same admin team, same principles, same website URL.

docs.title: What Didn't Carry Over
docs.text:
• Progress from the previous world. Everything is a fresh start.
  • Rewards / voting — not currently wired up on the new server. May return later.

docs.title: How to Join
docs.text: See the Install page for step-by-step instructions for every popular launcher.

docs.title: Reporting Issues
docs.text: Bug reports are welcome. See Support for how to reach an admin.

docs.title: Rules & Core Principles
docs.text:
The server runs on a small set of principles rather than a long rule list. If you understand these five, you understand how the server works — and how disputes get resolved.

The one hard boundary

Ideological views, dark humor, and heated arguments are tolerated. Targeted harassment is not. Slurs, threats, or sustained pile-ons directed at a specific person or group cross the line — everywhere else is fair game.

docs.title: 1. Radical Freedom
docs.text:
• PvP, building, and raiding are allowed everywhere.
  • No safe zones. No protected territories. No claim system.
  • If you don't want to lose it, don't leave it unattended.

docs.title: 2. Ideological Tolerance
docs.text:
• Extreme political and ideological views are permitted in global chat.
  • Hard boundary: no targeting groups or individuals with slurs, threats, or sustained harassment.

docs.title: 3. Death & Consequences
docs.text:
• Inventory drops fully on death — standard vanilla behavior.
  • Griefing, theft, and betrayal are legal. Trust is earned, not granted.

docs.title: 4. Absolute Independence
docs.text:
• The server has no official Discord, no official guilds, and no "partnered" communities.
  • Any group claiming to represent server administration is unofficial and unaffiliated.

docs.title: 5. Verified Authority
docs.text:
• Only two people have administrative power: Auzer1 and FunOD.
  • Anyone else claiming to be a moderator, "helper," or staff is lying.
  • We do not run hidden or alt staff accounts for moderation.

docs.title: Conflict Resolution
docs.text:
How disputes are actually handled when they escalate:

Situation Handling In-game conflict, chat drama, PvP grudges Chat/world isolation is the primary tool Evidence of off-server attacks (DMs, forums, doxxing attempts) Permanent cross-platform ban Impersonation of staff Immediate ban Reports without evidence Not actioned

docs.title: What Is Not a Rule
docs.text:
To save everyone time, these things are allowed and are not going to be actioned:

  • Killing other players, anywhere, for any reason
  • Building near, on top of, or inside another player's base
  • Stealing, scamming in trades, betraying alliances
  • Trash-talking in chat within the hard-boundary limits above
  • Using client-side mods that pass the AntiCheat (see FAQ)

If you're looking for a protected, moderated experience, this is not the right server for you — and that's fine.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text:
If you've lost your progress or forgotten your server login password, you can contact an admin directly.

Click to reveal contact

Discord: @auzer

Please mention that your issue is with the Cobblemon server specifically (there are a lot of Auzers out there, and we run more than one server).

docs.title: Reporting an Issue
docs.text:
Before reaching out, check whether your issue is covered on one of these pages:

  • Rules — for questions about what is and isn't allowed.
  • FAQ — for common questions about server operation and the modpack.
  • Install — for setup, launcher, and mod-list problems.
  • News — for downtime notices, updates, and known issues.

If none of those cover it, contact an admin using the spoiler above.

What we cannot help with

  • Player disputes (see Rules)
  • Issues with third-party launchers or your local Minecraft installation
  • The official Cobbleverse modpack — our modified pack is what runs here; see Install
